matchups.preview: Rilind's rolling out Week 1 with the same energy he brought to last year's collapse — absolutely zero self-awareness about how badly he's about to fuck this up. Rob's about to remind everyone why he's perennially trading players at 11:59pm on Sunday, desperately trying to salvage whatever dumpster fire he assembled in the draft. Two teams, zero wins, infinite ways to disappoint yourselves.

Jetmir and Peter are about to learn that drafting like you're playing a video game on easy mode doesn't fly in the real world, while Adam's about to show them what actual roster construction looks like—assuming he doesn't pull some galaxy-brain waiver move mid-week that fucks it all up for himself.

Ilir's got all the makings of a classic Week 1 collapse—overconfident after a decent draft, about to get humbled by a team that actually has a fucking gameplan. Rinor's rolling out there like he knows what he's doing, but we all know he's one injury away from panic trades and roster meltdowns. This is gonna be ugly, and whoever loses first is setting the tone for a long season of excuses.

Faton's about to get absolutely baptized by his own flesh and blood—Flamur's got the draft capital and the hunger, while Faton's rolling out there looking like he made his picks while blackout drunk at a wedding. Blood may be thicker than water, but it won't save Faton's ass from getting embarrassed on his family's own turf this week.

Veton's about to learn that drafting three running backs in the first four rounds doesn't make you a genius—it makes you broke at receiver. Arben's rolling in here with actual depth and a functioning brain, ready to expose whatever mid-tier WR wasteland Veton's cobbled together. This is gonna be ugly.

Ben's out here looking like he panic-drafted a kicker in round 4 before the season even started, while Nori's roster is held together with duct tape and false hope. Week 1 is going to expose both of you frauds, but at least one of you will limp away with a moral victory—spoiler alert: it won't be the guy who reached on a tight end when there were actual playmakers on the board.
